<reason>CON won a competitive debate by making the live clash easier to decide: the motion requires a first-claim, cheaper reserved stock, and PRO’s remaining principle (reciprocity after conceding passion and poverty) does not track disruption, need, or equal terms of competition. CON answered pressure directly, used PRO’s concessions, and offered a cleaner vote: one eligibility list versus a two-step club privilege. PRO had a coherent bounded-obligation case and a sharp Q2, but never escaped incidence, outsider cost, and empty-recognition-if-and-only-if-locked-inventory.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON’s Rebuttal 2: equal sale means equal terms, not equal wallets; loyalty without reserved cheaper stock is not a defect because nobody is owed that seat—then converting PRO’s reciprocity+lottery into a two-step privilege.</best_rebuttal>
